defects.defect: 51 dead `variant` props fleet-wide (5 in the subject file): glass-ui 7.0.0 Button has no `variant` prop, so the shadcn styling vocabulary that survived the Glass 7 adoption is silently discarded and leaks to the DOM as a literal attribute. The subject file speaks BOTH vocabularies 40 lines apart.
defects.evidence: node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/button/Button.vue.d.ts:6-19 — ButtonProps = { emphasis, tone, size, iconOnly, loading, type, disabled, class }; no `variant`. `grep -o "outline\|ghost" node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/button-Bu9F4uU6.js` → ZERO matches. `emphasis: { default: "secondary" }` in the same chunk. Subject file: variant="outline" at :22,:33,:58,:114 and variant="ghost" at :123 — while :174 `emphasis="text"` and :175 `:tone="confirmDestructive ? 'destructive' : 'neutral'"` are correct Glass 7. Live DOM (Playwright browser_evaluate on http://localhost:9000): `{"tag":"BUTTON","text":"Login","variant":"outline"}`, `{"text":"@mbabb","variant":"ghost"}`, `{"text":"Try again","variant":"outline"}`. Fleet script: 51 `<Button variant=...>` sites in 22 files, incl. FlagReportDialog.vue:41 `variant="destructive"` (a TONE passed as a dead variant). Gate is blind: `npx vue-tsc -p tsconfig.demo.json --noEmit` → exit 0, 0 errors.
defects.mechanism: Vue treats an unrecognised lowercase prop as an HTML fallthrough attribute, so a retired design-token vocabulary is neither type-checked nor visibly broken — it renders at the default `emphasis="secondary"` and ships the string to the DOM.
defects.reproduction: Load http://localhost:9000/#/admin/users and evaluate `[...document.querySelectorAll('button')].map(b=>b.getAttribute('variant'))` — `outline`/`ghost` appear as literal attributes. Design consequence at AdminUsersPanel.vue:107-111: the comment asserts the per-row destructive is 'quieted to ink-at-rest' via variant="ghost"; glass-ui discards it and renders `secondary`.
defects.proposedCure: Mechanical: variant="outline"→emphasis="secondary", variant="ghost"→emphasis="quiet", variant="destructive"→tone="destructive", variant="default"→emphasis="primary". Structurally the reason 51 sites drifted for a whole tranche is that nothing rejects an unknown token prop: glass-ui Button should set `inheritAttrs: false` with an explicit attr allowlist so an unrecognised design prop is a visible no-op. That half is a glass-ui change and belongs in the BH relay.

defects.defect: The unauthorized state is costumed as an empty roster — the exact F-2 invariant the component's own comment claims to have cured. The auth precondition is a route concern re-asserted 22× as per-method early returns, with no route guard anywhere.
defects.evidence: demo/palettes/useAdminUsers.ts:54-58 `const token = getAdminToken(); if (!token) return;` — returns without touching `loadingUsers` or `usersLoadError`. AdminUsersPanel.vue:63 `<EmptyState v-else-if="users.length === 0" eyebrow="· roster clear ·" message="No users found." />`. Certified screenshot docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/shots/safari-desktop-light/admin-users.png: dock reads 'Login' (unauthenticated), panel reads '· ROSTER CLEAR · / No users found.' REPORT.json for that row: consoleErrors [], pageErrors [], bodyTextLength 273, counts.button 15 — all four matrices identical. Component comment AdminUsersPanel.vue:49-50 states the violated invariant verbatim: 'error ≠ empty — a dead backend never costumes as an empty roster.' `grep -c 'if (!token)' demo/palettes/useAdminUsers.ts` = 11; `grep -rn --include='*.ts' 'if (!token)' demo/ | wc -l` = 22 across 5 admin composables. No guard: grep over demo/shell/ for beforeEnter|requiresAdmin|guard on admin views = 0 hits; demo/shell/viewSchema.ts:188 declares "admin-users" with no auth meta.
defects.mechanism: An authorization precondition that belongs once at the route boundary is modelled as a silent early return inside every data method, so the view can never distinguish 'no data' from 'not allowed' — the panel models 3 states where the domain has 4.
defects.reproduction: Open http://localhost:9000/#/admin/users with no admin session (the state the whole certified visual matrix was captured in). The full admin console renders and affirmatively reports '· ROSTER CLEAR · / No users found.' with zero console errors — see the four safari-* admin-users.png shots and their REPORT.json rows.
defects.proposedCure: One gate at the composition boundary: an `<AdminGate>` in AdminPane.vue (or an `auth: "admin"` flag in viewSchema honoured by one guard in useViewManager) rendering an authentication plate when `!isAdminAuthenticated`. Inside the gate `getAdminToken()` is a non-null contract and all 22 `if (!token) return` guards delete; the panel never needs an unauthorized state because it never mounts unauthorized.

defects.defect: PaletteCard feeds arbitrary user/API color strings into `certifyAccentInk`, a demo-side wrapper that converts the library's typed Result error into a thrown exception during render. Any palette color carrying alpha < 1 destroys the whole hosting pane via the error boundary; zero cards render and the poison is persisted in localStorage.
defects.evidence: PaletteCard.vue:226 `firstColor = props.palette.colors[0]?.css ?? …`; PaletteCard.vue:229-230 `const { safeCss } = useSafeAccentFn("well"); const safeFirstColor = computed(() => safeCss(firstColor.value))`; demo/color-session/ink.ts:78 `if (!result.ok) throw new Error(`Ink certification failed: ${result.error.code}`)`; src/color/operations.ts:213-214 `if (accent.alpha !== 1 || surface.alpha !== 1) return err({ code: "color_invalid_input" })`. node against the served dist: `lab(50% 20 10 / 82.7%) => safeAccent ERR color_invalid_input`, `oklch(0.7 0.1 200 / 0.5) => ERR color_invalid_input`, `#e11d48 => OK`. Live: pane shows `This panel hit an unexpected error. / color_non_finite`, articles: 0. The app's own persisted state held `color-picker = {"inputColor":"lab(92% 88.8 20 / 82.7%)"}`, i.e. it mints alpha'd colors itself.
defects.mechanism: Ownership inversion at the library boundary: the library owns 'certification may fail, here is a typed error'; demo/color-session/ink.ts unilaterally re-declares it as 'cannot fail' and PaletteCard consumes that re-declaration on untrusted data. A total function was made partial at the wrong layer.
defects.reproduction: With the dev server live at http://localhost:9000: (1) in the page, `localStorage.setItem('color-palettes', JSON.stringify({version:1,palettes:[{id:'p',slug:'p',name:'Probe',isLocal:true,colors:[{css:'lab(50% 20 10 / 82.7%)',position:0},{css:'#0ea5e9',position:1}]}]}))`; (2) full reload of `/#/palettes`, settle 2s. Observed `{url:'http://localhost:9000/#/palettes', boundary:true, bodyHead:'…This panel hit an unexpected error.\n\ncolor_non_finite…', articles:0}`. Repeats with `lab(92% 88.8 20 / 82.7%)`. Control with `['#e11d48','#0ea5e9']` → no boundary. (Exact throw site among ink.ts:47/59/78 is a hypothesis; the Result-to-throw class is confirmed.)
defects.proposedCure: Make `certifyAccentInk` TOTAL on dynamic input — return the input css (or the muted-ink token) for every non-certifiable value, exactly as it already does for unparseable input at ink.ts:136, and add the alpha pre-condition the library states at operations.ts:214. Keep throws only for producer literals (ink.ts:53), which are build-time invariants. Then no ink consumer can crash a pane and PaletteCard needs no guard at all.

defects.defect: Non-concentric corner: the full-bleed colour strip carries the card's OUTER 16px radius while sitting at the border's INNER edge, where 14px is required. Together with three stacked zero-blur casters this is the mechanism behind the owner's own mark, which the prior seat's report never references.
defects.evidence: Measured live: card `border-top-left-radius: 16px`, `border-top-width: 2px`, strip inset from card left = `2px` (i.e. exactly at the inner edge), strip `border-top-left-radius: 16px`. Concentric requirement = 16 − 2 = **14px**. Owner artifact: `docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/owner-marked/OM-2-card-shadow-sharp-corners.png`. Shadow half, computed: `oklab(0.28 …/0.32) -3px 3px 0px 0px, oklab(0.28 …/0.26) -5px 5px 0px 0px, oklab(0.28 …/0.18) -7px 7px 0px 0px` — three hard copies, zero blur, zero spread. Radius applied at PaletteCard.vue:36 (`rounded-t-card`), forced by the deliberate refusal of overflow-hidden at :16-18.
defects.mechanism: Clip responsibility was moved onto the child (to avoid 1-bit rasterization at compositing-layer bounds) without moving the radius arithmetic with it. Three copies of a 16px arc at three offsets diverge maximally at the rounds and converge along the straight edges, so the cast reads clean on the sides and faceted/stepped at the corners.
defects.reproduction: http://localhost:9000/#/palettes with any populated palette; read `border-top-left-radius`/`border-top-width` on `[role="article"]` and `border-top-left-radius` + `getBoundingClientRect().left` delta on its strip child. Visual: owner-marked/OM-2-card-shadow-sharp-corners.png.
defects.proposedCure: The concentric arithmetic should never be authored by hand. Cure step 1 (`<Card … :shadow="false">`) removes the three casters and therefore the visible artefact; the strip radius then belongs to a producer-side inner-radius token (`calc(var(--radius-card) - var(--card-border-width))`) rather than a repeated `rounded-t-card` literal at the consumer.

defects.defect: In dark mode the cel shadow is effectively the same luminance as the surface casting it, and the alpha was raised to compensate rather than the contrast fixed.
defects.evidence: Measured on the same element, light vs `.dark`: card `background-color` `oklab(0.913 …)` → `oklab(0.345 …)`; shadow colour `oklab(0.28 …)` → `oklab(0.34 …)`; alphas .32/.26/.18 → **.46/.38/.26**. L(shadow) − L(card) = **−0.633 light** vs **−0.005 dark**. Token: `--shadow-cartoon-md` uses `light-dark(hsl(24 10% 10%), hsl(30 14% 90%))` then `clamp(0.28, l, 0.34)`, so the dark arm takes the LIGHT source colour and clamps it down to 0.34 — landing on the card's own 0.345.
defects.mechanism: A hard-edged cel shadow requires luminance headroom beneath the surface; a dark card has none, so the register degrades to a grey smear whose only surviving signal is the offset silhouette. The alpha bump from .32 to .46 is evidence someone noticed the weak read and compensated with opacity instead of contrast.
defects.reproduction: http://localhost:9000/#/palettes; read `boxShadow` and `backgroundColor` on `[role="article"]`, then `document.documentElement.classList.add('dark')` and read both again.
defects.proposedCure: Not a token patch — the ruled tuple already says `shadow: false` for this species (VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §3.1). Cure step 1 removes the caster entirely; a matte specimen slip needs no cast shadow on either scheme. If any producer follow-up is warranted it is a letter to glass-ui that `--shadow-cartoon-md`'s dark arm clamps into its own surface band.

defects.defect: The identity row has no overflow design in any direction: once the title is starved to 0 (D-2), the remaining `shrink-0` content exits the card box and then the viewport. The prior seat measured a 37px chip↔menu overlap; the mechanism is unbounded.

defects.mechanism: Title absorbs 100% of negative free space (line-clamp's overflow:hidden zeroes its automatic minimum), reaches 0, and the remaining unshrinkable content simply overflows. `REPORT.md`'s `horizontalOverflow: 0` misses it because an ancestor clips before the document scroll width grows — the content is lost, not merely off-screen.

defects.proposedCure: Structural, per the ruled anatomy: the identity line gets its own row with `flex-1 min-w-0` and the meta cluster is demoted below it or behind a single count — the chips stop being peers of the title. This is the same move that cures D-2, D-5 and D-18, and it is why `PaletteCardMeta` must not exist as a bare multi-root fragment of `shrink-0` siblings spliced into the parent's flex row. defects.defect: `ActionFeedback` never re-arms its dismissal timer and never clears it on unmount. Because `showFeedback` sets an already-true `visible` ref, the watcher does not fire and the new message inherits the previous message's remaining countdown; and no `onUnmounted` cleanup exists, so a pending timeout fires into a destroyed component and writes to a dead card's state.

defects.reproduction: `npx vitest run --config <probe cfg>` on a mount of ActionFeedback via a host replicating PaletteCard's wiring: showFeedback('Saved!','success'); advanceTimersByTime(2400); showFeedback('Delete failed','error'); advanceTimersByTime(100) → visible === false. Second test: showFeedback then unmount() → vi.getTimerCount() still 1.
defects.proposedCure: The component is a timed toast, so the boolean is the wrong subject: watch message identity (`() => [props.visible, props.message]`) and register `onUnmounted(() => clearTimeout(timer))`. Better still, hoist the dismissal to the caller and let ActionFeedback be pure presentation — that also removes the `update:visible` round-trip back into the parent.

defects.defect: `defineExpose({ showFeedback })` forces both consumers to maintain a component-instance map, and both register it with `:ref="(el: any) => el && (cardRefs[key] = el)"`. Vue calls a function ref with `null` on unmount, so the `el &&` guard makes teardown a no-op: nothing is ever deleted. The reactive map grows for the session lifetime, retaining dead component instances and, through them, whole subtrees, spring instances, hover closures and Palette objects.

defects.mechanism: an imperative `defineExpose` handle as the feedback channel forces an identity map on every host; the `el &&` truthiness guard silently discards Vue's unmount signal, and the `(el: any)` cast hides the null from tsc
defects.reproduction: NONE — code-level certainty rather than an executed measurement (the shared dev browser in this formation had a concurrent writer, so a live key count would not have been attributable). The omission is unambiguous: Vue invokes function refs with `null` on unmount and the guard drops that call.
defects.proposedCure: Architectural transposition, not a delete-key fix: make feedback DATA. Lift `{ key, message, variant }` into the pane and pass it down as a prop (`:feedback="feedback?.key === palette.slug ? feedback : null"`). `defineExpose`, both cardRefs maps, both `(el: any)` casts and the leak all disappear together, and the component stops needing an imperative handle at all.

defects.defect: useHoverPopover reads `e.currentTarget` inside a nextTick callback — i.e. after event dispatch has completed, when the DOM spec guarantees it is null. Spec: DOM Standard §2.2 — "The currentTarget attribute … When an event is dispatched, this is set to the object whose listener is being invoked, and reset to null afterwards."

defects.proposedCure: Capture the element at dispatch time (`const el = e.currentTarget as Element` BEFORE nextTick) is the patch; the transposition is to delete the branch — let the design-system Popover anchor to its own trigger so no coordinate is ever computed in demo/ at all.

defects.defect: useHeightTransition's onAfterEnter calls scrollIntoView({behavior:"smooth"}), which by spec bypasses the app's global prefers-reduced-motion guard: every card expansion smooth-scrolls the page for a user who asked for reduced motion.
defects.evidence: demo/palettes/browser/card/composables/useHeightTransition.ts:48 — `htmlEl.scrollIntoView({ behavior: "smooth", block: "nearest" });`. The guard at demo/styles/animations.css:184-192 sets `scroll-behavior: auto !important` on `*`. CSSOM-View defers to the CSS scroll-behavior property only when the `behavior` option is "auto"; an explicit "smooth" forces a smooth scroll regardless. (The same composable's inline `style.transition` writes ARE caught, by the !important duration override — so the guard works everywhere except where JS overrides it explicitly.)
defects.mechanism: A height-morph composable that also performs document navigation — two unrelated responsibilities in one seam, and the second one escapes the CSS-level motion policy.

defects.defect: useHoverPopover computes `left = rect.left + rect.width/2` — a CENTRE coordinate — but leaves the required translateX(-50%) to its consumers, and only one of the two supplies it.

defects.mechanism: Split ownership: the correction that makes the composable's output mean what it computes is not owned by the composable (nor by SwatchHoverMenu, the single component that consumes floatingStyle).
defects.reproduction: NONE — currently unobservable because L-15/L-16 destroy the position entirely. This is a LATENT defect that becomes live the moment those two are cured.
defects.proposedCure: Either return a left-edge coordinate, or fold the -50% into the composable's returned style object. Better: the design-system Popover anchors itself and no centering arithmetic exists anywhere.

defects.defect: The confirmation dialog for the irreversible "Prune empty" bulk deletion states a count derived from the search-FILTERED client list, while the action it guards is an unscoped server-wide mutation. It promises fewer deletions than it performs.
defects.evidence: demo/palettes/browser/admin/AdminUsersPanel.vue:241 (emptyCount over the `users` prop) + demo/palettes/admin/AdminPane.vue:28 (users = pm.filteredAdminUsers) + demo/palettes/useAdminUsers.ts:29-48 (filtered+sorted) vs demo/palettes/useAdminUsers.ts:190 (pruneEmptyUsers(token) — no scope arg). Probe output: D-filtered {"headerBadge":"6","toolbar":["6 users","· 1 empty"],"renderedRows":1}; D-dialog "Prune 1 empty users?\n\nThis will permanently delete 1 user with 0 palettes and their sessions. This cannot be undone."; D-after POST /admin/users/prune-empty → toolbarAfter ["Pruned 3 users"]. Frame docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/AdminUsersPanel/frames-D2/D-confirm-prune-filtered-dark.png. Aggravated by demo/palettes/useAdminUsers.ts:59 listUsers(token, 50) — even unfiltered the number is a 50-row page count. Law: VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:218 ("dangerous confirmation … Actor, scope, provenance and effect remain visible"); PROPORTION-AUDIT.md:55 PR-11.
defects.mechanism: Truth derived at the wrong altitude: the leaf computes scope from whatever array it was handed instead of receiving the server's scope.
defects.reproduction: node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/AdminUsersPanel/probe-D2.mjs (section D). Manually: #/admin/users with an admin token and ≥2 empty users, type a query matching exactly ONE empty user, click "Prune empty", read the dialog, confirm, read the result line.
defects.proposedCure: Confirm against the server's scope, not a client-derived count: the prune affordance resolves the candidate set (GET the empty users), the dialog NAMES the candidates, and the confirmed call carries those identities — the two-phase review anatomy PR-11 already prescribes. Reading the unfiltered array instead only swaps a wrong number for a differently wrong one, because that array is a 50-row page.

defects.defect: A failed destructive mutation renders as a benign, self-contradicting success message. A 500 on the prune endpoint produces "No empty users to prune" while the same toolbar simultaneously reads "· 2 empty". No error surface at all.
defects.evidence: demo/palettes/useAdminUsers.ts:195-198 (catch → return 0) meeting demo/palettes/browser/admin/AdminUsersPanel.vue:303-309 (count > 0 ? "Pruned N" : "No empty users to prune"). Probe output with the endpoint fulfilled 500 application/problem+json: {"message":"No empty users to prune","toolbar":["3 users","· 2 empty"],"rowsStillRendered":3,"anyErrorRole":false}. Frame frames-D2/G-prune-FAILED-desktop-light.png. The component already ratified the opposite principle for the LOAD path at AdminUsersPanel.vue:49-50 ("error ≠ empty — a dead backend never costumes as an empty roster") and :51-62 (EmptyState variant="error").
defects.mechanism: The result channel's type cannot express failure: onPruneDone(count: number) collapses {refused} and {nothing to do} into the same integer, so no downstream design can distinguish them.
defects.reproduction: node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/AdminUsersPanel/probe-D2d-prune-failure.mjs — intercepts POST **/prune-empty with a 500 and reads the rendered result span.
defects.proposedCure: Widen the result to the three outcomes the action actually has (pruned N / nothing to prune / failed + machine reason) and render failure in the error register already ratified at :51-62. The signature, not the string, is the defect.

defects.defect: Concurrent-expand race: `toggleUserExpand` writes `userPalettes` from an awaited fetch with no request-generation guard, so a late response for user A renders inside user B's open disclosure — and the admin delete then destroys A's palette while decrementing B's count.
defects.evidence: demo/palettes/browser/admin/AdminUsersPanel.vue:352-365 (`userPalettes.value = await pm.loadUserPalettes(slug)`; `finally` clears loading first-to-settle) and :150 (`@admin-delete="emit('adminDeleteUserPalette', $event, user.slug)"`). probe-impl-c3.json, BOTH engines identical: `t_betaSettled: {openRow: "beta-drifter-00022Pale", disclosure: "BETA-PALETTE-BBB 2 0"}` then `t_alphaLanded: {openRow: "beta-drifter-00022Pale", disclosure: "ALPHA-PALETTE-AAA 2 0"}`, `RACE_REPRODUCED: true`. probe-impl-c3b.json: `deleteRequests: ["http://localhost:9077/admin/palettes/alpha-p-1"]`, `VERDICT: {betaBadgeBefore:"2", betaBadgeAfter:"1", alphaBadgeBefore:"4", alphaBadgeAfter:"4"}`. useAdminUsers.ts:118-121 decrements the owner passed by the row. Frames: frames-impl/C3b-{chromium,webkit}-beta-shows-alpha.png.
defects.mechanism: Value not bound to its key — `expandedUserSlug` and `userPalettes` are two independent cells joined only by wall-clock order; nothing records which request a resolved value belongs to.
defects.reproduction: VITE_API_URL=http://localhost:9077 npx vite --port 9077 ; node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/AdminUsersPanel/probe-impl-c3.mjs (race, 2 engines) ; node .../probe-impl-c3b.mjs (the destroying DELETE + badge deltas). Serve alpha's /admin/users/*/palettes with 1500ms delay and beta's with 40ms; click alpha, wait 300ms, click beta.
defects.proposedCure: Do not add a sequence counter to the current shape — the shape is the defect. Express the disclosure as the keyed resource it is: a colocated `useAdminUserPalettes(slugRef)` driven by `watch(slugRef, …)` with an AbortController cancelled on key change, returning `{ palettes, loading, error }` bound to the key they were fetched for. A response for a stale key then has nowhere to land — the race becomes unrepresentable rather than policed. Side effects: supplies C-4's missing `error` cell, and removes userPalettes/removeUserPalette/updatePaletteTier/clearUserPalettes from the :389 defineExpose (the adjudicated L-1/L-2 inversion) as a consequence rather than as separate work.

This will permanently delete 1 user with 0 palettes and their sessions. This cannot be undone."`. Renaming the computed or passing the unfiltered array does not fix the split; the description and the effect must be the same query. result.strongestDefect: D-01 — a single click on BrowsePane's own Retry button permanently destroys the pane body. `<Transition name="vj-morph" mode="out-in">` (BrowsePane.vue:40) couples DOM presence to a 200ms animation clock, while the state machine it animates settles synchronously (assertApiAttemptAllowed throws before any fetch, availability.ts:188-195). defects.defect: One Retry click permanently blanks the pane body. Transition mode="out-in" on the three-state container makes DOM presence a function of a 200ms animation clock, while the state machine settles synchronously; the pending enter never mounts and the pane is left as a void under the search field with no error, no empty plate, no skeleton and no recovery.
defects.evidence: demo/palettes/BrowsePane.vue:40 (`<Transition name="vj-morph" mode="out-in">`); demo/platform/transport/availability.ts:188-195 (assertApiAttemptAllowed throws synchronously, unconditional for `misconfigured`). Live Playwright/WebKit 1440x900, sampled every 25ms from the click: t=0 n=1 h=224.5 "The commons is unreachable.Failed to load palettes"; t=28 n=1 vj-morph-leave-from|vj-morph-leave-active; t=227 n=1 vj-morph-leave-active|vj-morph-leave-to; t=251 n=0 h=12.0 ""; t=1202 n=0 h=12.0 "". Screenshots: docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/BrowsePane/evidence/D-browse-before-retry.png vs D-browse-after-retry-6s.png.
defects.mechanism: Animation clock owns DOM presence — branch identity is animated with mode="out-in" across an async boundary that can settle faster than the leave duration.
defects.reproduction: 1) `http://localhost:9000/#/browse` at 1440x900 (dev server without VITE_API_URL, so the misconfigured latch is armed — the state all 60 audit captures show). 2) Wait ~3.5s for the error plate. 3) Click Retry once. 4) The state container's element children go 1→0 at ~251ms and stay 0 indefinitely; wrapper height 224.5px→12px. defects.proposedCure: Stop animating branch identity. Keep one persistent state region whose CONTENT cross-fades (default simultaneous mode), or drop the Transition on the state container entirely and let the individual plates own their entrance. defects.defect: `.search-seated` is a per-instance override of a glass-ui root component, deliberately unlayered to beat the producer's cascade layer, and replicated across three consumers — a producer variant that was never raised.
defects.evidence: Owner edicts 4 and 5. BrowsePane.vue:12 applies class="search-seated" to SearchBar from @mkbabb/glass-ui/search. demo/styles/utils.css:132-155 overrides background, backdrop-filter, border, box-shadow, max-width and the descendant `.input-bar-field` font-family; its own comment: "INTERIM DEMO SEAT — a consumer opt-in on the producer recipe (unlayered, so it wins over the @layer components recipe by layer order) … BOOKED SWAP … dies onto glass-ui's P3 seated field-chrome rung — ASK-D (variant=\"seated\")". Site census: BrowsePane.vue:12, PalettesPane.vue:35, admin/AdminPane.vue:14.
defects.mechanism: Producer boundary crossed — three consumers of one hand-rolled chrome, using cascade-layer ordering as the override mechanism edict 5 exists to forbid.
defects.reproduction: grep -rn "search-seated" demo/ → three .vue consumers plus the utils.css definition; read utils.css:132-155 for the override surface.
defects.proposedCure: Land `variant="seated"` in glass-ui SearchBar (ASK-D, already filed) and delete the three-site override plus the utils.css block. Booked is not shipped.

defects.defect: "Find by Color" is a silent partial search over the loaded page while the server API supports the query, with an untokenised magic radius and a silent data-dependent exclusion.
defects.evidence: BrowsePane.vue:336-355 — `const radius = 0.15;` then a client-side filter over pm.filteredBrowse with `if (!oklabColors || oklabColors.length === 0) return false;` and the comment "API also supports server-side via colorL/colorA/colorB params, but client-side is instant". demo/palettes/api/palettes.ts:49-52 genuinely sends colorL/colorA/colorB/colorRadius. BROWSE_PAGE_SIZE is 50, and BrowsePane.vue:133 keys load-more on pm.hasMore, so paging fetches the next UNFILTERED page and then colour-filters it. `oklabColors` is optional on the type (types.ts:32) and is a migration field server-side (api/src/platform/migrations/check.ts:46). The `(p: any)` cast at :344 is unnecessary since oklabColors is declared on Palette.
defects.mechanism: Search semantics unowned — a masking client-side fallback chosen over a working server path (owner edict 2), plus an unparameterised distance threshold.
defects.reproduction: NONE for the runtime arm (needs a populated reachable commons). Code-proven: the server params exist and are unused; the radius is a bare literal; the missing-oklabColors branch returns false.
defects.proposedCure: Use the server colour params so the search covers the commons; token the radius and expose it or justify it against a measured OKLab ΔE; render palettes lacking oklabColors as an explicit excluded count rather than dropping them into a false empty.

defects.defect: cardRefs is a deep-reactive map of component public instances whose entries are never released, because the ref callback's `el &&` guard skips the unmount null.
defects.evidence: BrowsePane.vue:209 `const cardRefs = reactive<Record<string, InstanceType<typeof PaletteCard>>>({});` and :94 `:ref="(el: any) => el && (cardRefs[palette.slug] = el)"`. Vue invokes the function ref with null on unmount; the guard skips that call, so no key is ever deleted. `reactive` (not shallowReactive/markRaw) means each read returns a reactive proxy wrapping a component public instance, so property access is tracked inside the component's own instance graph. `grep -rn "shallowReactive|markRaw" demo/palettes/` → zero hits.
defects.mechanism: Local hygiene — imperative child-instance coupling stored in the wrong reactivity primitive with no teardown.
defects.reproduction: NONE for the accumulation arm — requires a reachable API to populate and page the wall past the 50-cap. Labelled a hypothesis on runtime consequence; the code shape (no delete path, deep reactive) is confirmed.
defects.proposedCure: Delete the ref map entirely — the feedback it drives belongs in the inspector D-03 is missing (see D-17). If a collection must survive, use a plain Map with an explicit null-branch delete.

defects.defect: Transient per-card feedback is the ONLY truth for save, delete, visibility and fork outcomes, and it is silently swallowed if the card unmounted between request and verdict.
defects.evidence: BrowsePane.vue:226-250 and :262-265 route every verdict through cardRefs[slug].showFeedback(...) (PaletteCard.vue:238,244 defineExpose). :249 uses optional chaining, so a verdict for an unmounted card is discarded with no surface. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md §5: "Persistent operation state stays with the entity/workspace. A transient flourish may celebrate success but never carries the only truth."
defects.mechanism: Failure/pending truth is absent or false — same PR-08 family as D-07/D-08.
defects.reproduction: NONE — code-proven; the swallow path requires a reachable API plus a filter/sort/page change between request and response.
defects.proposedCure: Durable per-entity operation state in the selected inspector (the region D-03 identifies as missing); the flourish may remain, but only as celebration over a persisted truth.

defects.defect: The route has no H1; the pane identity announces as h3 with no h2 or h1 above it, while being styled at the display-1 rung the type matrix reserves for the route H1.
defects.evidence: REPORT.json /#/browse, all four matrices: "h1": 0, "main": 1. Live accessibility snapshot: `heading "Browse" [level=3]`. demo/shared/ui/PaneHeader.vue emits `<h3 class="pane-header-title font-display">` and styles it `.pane-header-title { font-size: var(--type-display-1) }`. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md §4.1: "Each route has one H1 and exactly one stable main landmark, owned by the shell"; §4 maps route H1 to text-display/Fraunces.
defects.mechanism: Local hygiene / shared-atom family — PaneHeader has 9 consumers; the cure belongs at the shell plus that atom, BrowsePane is a site.
defects.reproduction: Load /#/browse and evaluate `document.querySelectorAll('h1').length` → 0; the visually-largest text on the pane is an h3.
defects.proposedCure: The shell owns the route H1 per §4.1; PaneHeader emits the correct level beneath it, or the pane identity becomes the H1 when the pane is the route protagonist.

defects.defect: Two hard-coded skeleton counts (4 and 2) for one grammar, neither related to the 50-row page size, so the skeleton is decoration rather than a request-shaped preview.
defects.evidence: BrowsePane.vue:207 `const SKELETON_COUNT = 4;` and :130 `<PaletteCardSkeleton v-for="i in 2" ...>` — the second is a bare literal with no name. BROWSE_PAGE_SIZE is 50 (useBrowsePalettes.ts currentFilterOpts). VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md §7: "Request-bound skeletons exist only while real work is in flight."
defects.mechanism: Local hygiene — two magic numbers for one designed grammar.
defects.reproduction: Read BrowsePane.vue:130 and :207.
defects.proposedCure: One named count derived from the page size (or a deliberate, documented cap) shared by both arms; the constitution's grammar is one species, so it should read from one source.

defects.defect: The forced-colors capture proves nothing (WebKit does not honour the emulation) and the pane ships no forced-colors treatment, so the selection/focus deltas §4.1 and §4.2 require are undemonstrated.
defects.evidence: shots/forced-colors-desktop/browse.png is visually indistinguishable from shots/safari-desktop-light/browse.png apart from a slightly muted ambient field — glass cards still translucent, the pastel `Palettes` gradient text still renders, cartoon shadows still paint. Repo-wide `grep -rn forced-colors demo/ src/` → 9 hits, all in demo/styles/foundation.css, demo/styles/focus-ring.css and one gradient editor; ZERO under demo/palettes/. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md §4.1: focus distinct from selection "in both schemes, forced colors and reduced transparency"; §4.2 requires a nonzero selected-state delta in forced colors.
defects.mechanism: Local hygiene / evidence gap — an unverified matrix cited as coverage.
defects.reproduction: Compare the two PNGs side by side; then grep demo/palettes/ for forced-colors → no hits.
defects.proposedCure: Capture forced-colors on an engine that honours it (Chromium/Edge WHCM) before citing the matrix; then prove a nonzero selected-state and focus delta for the pane's selection model — which per D-03 is currently geometry-only card expansion.
